mainTopic: Why ״עָלֶיהָ״ is needed: limiting the מגו, the הקש of רבי יונה, and רבא's view that a ערוה needs no פסוק
overview: The גמרא first shows that the מגו idea (since יבום permits אשת אח, it should also permit אחות אשה) only works in a narrow case. That case is where the deceased brother married, died, and only then the living brother married the sister. It supports this from עולא's case of a מצורע who saw קרי on the night before his eighth day: a מגו needs a real moment when the thing was permitted. So ״עָלֶיהָ״ is needed for that one case. Alternatively, ״עָלֶיהָ״ is needed because רבי יונה's הקש would otherwise permit all עריות in יבום. When רב אחא מדפתי asks why we compare them to אחות אשה and not to אשת אח, the גמרא gives two answers: we go strict, and two prohibitions are learned from two. רבא then says a ערוה needs no פסוק at all, since an עשה cannot override a כרת prohibition, so the פסוק must be about the צרה. The גמרא defends him against several ברייתות, and רב אשי supports him from the משנה's wording. Finally, the גמרא asks why the צרה should need a פסוק either. רב אחא בר ביבי מר reports that in רבא's name, even the צרה needs no פסוק, and the real purpose of the פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The מגו works when the deceased brother married first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that the מגו makes sense when the deceased brother married first and the living brother married the sister afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well when the deceased brother married first and then the living brother married her sister. Since the איסור of אשת אח was permitted through יבום, the איסור of אחות אשה is also permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא grants the case where the earlier מגו argument works. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the איסור of אשת אח came first, and the איסור of אחות אשה was added on top of it later. Since יבום removes the first איסור, it makes sense to say the second one is removed together with it. The word תינח signals that a case where it does not work is about to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (setting up a contrast)
Since; the reasoning 'since X is permitted, Y is permitted too'
A brother's wife, normally forbidden
A wife's sister, normally forbidden
Was permitted

steps.confusionAlert: מת and חי here do not describe the situation at the time of marriage. מת is the brother who will later die childless, and חי is the brother who will remain alive to do יבום.

phrases.english: It works well where the deceased one married first
phrases.notes: "The deceased one" is the brother who later died without children; "the living one" is the brother left to do יבום.

phrases.english: and afterward the living one married her sister.
For since the prohibition of a brother's wife was permitted,
the prohibition of a wife's sister is also permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח הֵיכָא דְּנָשָׂא מֵת וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָשָׂא חַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a limitation of the מגו argument raised just before this section of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier claim that a מגו would let יבום permit אחות אשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: first grants the one case where the מגו fits, before showing where it fails.

steps.title: When the living brother married first, אחות אשה came first
steps.stepSummary: If the living brother married first, the איסור of אחות אשה came before the איסור of אשת אח, so the מגו does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the living brother married first and then the deceased brother married her sister, the איסור of אחות אשה came first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows a case where the מגו fails: the order of the marriages is reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here she was already forbidden as אחות אשה before she ever became אשת אח. When יבום removes the later איסור, there is no reason the older, earlier איסור should disappear with it. So the מגו cannot cover this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes first, precedes
But (introducing the problem case)

phrases.english: But if the living one married first,
and afterward the deceased one married her sister,
the prohibition of a wife's sister comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא נָשָׂא חַי, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָשָׂא מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תינח/אלא contrast begun in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The general reach of the מגו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מגו can remove a later איסור together with the one it rides on, but it cannot remove an איסור that existed earlier.

steps.title: Even when the deceased brother married first, she must have been permitted in between
steps.stepSummary: Even when the deceased brother married first, the מגו only works if he died before the living brother married the sister, so that she was permitted for a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even when the deceased brother married first, it only works where he married, then died, and afterward the living brother married her sister, because she was fit for him in between. But if the deceased brother married and had not yet died when the living brother married her sister, she was never fit for him at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the מגו even further, so that it works only if there was a moment when she was permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the deceased brother died first, there was a window when she was free of both איסורים, so it is reasonable to say the later איסור of אחות אשה does not take hold firmly. But if the deceased brother was still alive when the living brother married her sister, the two איסורים joined together with no gap at all. In that case there was no moment of permission to build the מגו on.

keyTerms.meaning: She was fit (permitted) for him
In between; the time gap
At all

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea of the section: a מגו needs at least one moment when the thing was actually permitted.

phrases.english: And even where the deceased one married first,
it works well where the deceased one married and died,
and afterward the living one married her sister,
because she was fit for him in between.
phrases.notes: He means the gap between the brother's death and the living brother's marriage to her sister.

phrases.english: But if the deceased one married and had not yet died,
and afterward the living one married her sister,
she was never fit for him at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, narrower limitation on top of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The מגו even in the order where the deceased brother married first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מגו requires a moment of real permission, and that moment is missing if the deceased brother was alive when the living brother married her sister.

steps.title: Proof from עולא: a מצורע who saw קרי on the night before the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that a מגו needs a moment of fitness: even עולא agrees that a מצורע who saw קרי on the night of the eighth may not put his hands in for the בהונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't עולא agree that if he saw קרי on the night of the eighth day, he may not insert his hands for the thumbs, because he never left his טומאה at a time when the day was fit for bringing a קרבן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from עולא's own rule to show that a מגו fails when there was never a moment of permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא allowed a מצורע who saw קרי on the eighth day itself to put his hands into the עזרה, using a מגו. But if he saw קרי the night before, there was never a daytime moment when he was fit to bring his קרבן, so the מגו does not apply. This matches step 3: with no window of permission, there is no מגו.

keyTerms.meaning: A seminal emission, which makes a person טמא
The night before the eighth day
The right thumb and big toe, where the מצורע receives the blood and oil
An offering

steps.whatToRemember: A מגו ("since this is permitted, that is permitted too") only works if there was at least one moment when the thing was actually permitted. Without that window, as in the מצורע who saw קרי the night before, the מגו falls away.

phrases.english: Doesn't עולא agree
that if he saw קרי on the night of the eighth,
phrases.notes: "He" is the מצורע finishing his purification. The night comes before the eighth day, when he would bring his קרבן.

phrases.english: that he may not insert his hands for the thumbs,
because he did not leave his impurity at a time
that is fit for bringing an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the point of step 3 with a parallel case.
steps.raayaObject: That a מגו requires a moment when the thing was permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's agreement about a מצורע who saw קרי on the night of the eighth

steps.title: The word 'with her' is needed for the case where the brother died before the sister was married
steps.stepSummary: After narrowing the מגו in the earlier steps, the גמרא concludes that ״עָלֶיהָ״ is needed for the one case where the מגו could have worked: the deceased married, died, and then the living brother married the sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the word 'with her' is needed for the case where the deceased brother married, then died, and only afterward the living brother married the sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now names the exact case where the תורה needed to write ״עָלֶיהָ״. It is the one case left standing after the earlier steps cut away the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this order of events, the brother's widow was permitted to the living brother for a while, before he married her sister. That moment of being permitted is what lets a מגו start, so we might have said 'since she is permitted, she stays permitted.' ״עָלֶיהָ״ comes to say no: she is still forbidden as his wife's sister.

keyTerms.meaning: 'With her' (ויקרא 18:18), the word that forbids a wife's sister even in a יבום case
The deceased brother married
The living brother married
And afterward; the order of events is what matters here

steps.whatToRemember: Without ״עָלֶיהָ״, a מגו would only have worked in one case: the dead brother married first, died, and only then the living brother married the sister. That gap gave a real moment when the widow was permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step brings the moment-of-fitness idea from Step 4 to its practical result. It is the only setup where ״עָלֶיהָ״ is truly needed to block a מגו.

phrases.english: Rather: when "with her" is necessary,
it is where the deceased one married, and then died,
and afterward the living one married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the proof in Step 4 (a מגו needs a moment of fitness) to pin down the only case where ״עָלֶיהָ״ is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought ״עָלֶיהָ״ is not needed at all, since the מגו fails in most orders of events
steps.terutzMaskana: ״עָלֶיהָ״ is needed for the case where the deceased married and died before the living brother married the sister, because there the מגו would otherwise have worked

steps.title: A second reason: רבי יונה's comparison would have permitted all forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: Another reason ״עָלֶיהָ״ is needed: the הקש of רבי יונה compares all עריות to אשת אח. Since אשת אח is permitted in יבום, we might have thought all עריות are too, so the תורה wrote ״עָלֶיהָ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say it comes from רבי יונה's comparison. The verse lists all the forbidden relations together with a brother's wife. Just as a brother's wife is permitted in יבום, so too all forbidden relations would be permitted. So the תורה wrote 'with her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different reason the תורה needed ״עָלֶיהָ״. Here the danger is a הקש, not a מגו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק puts all the עריות together, so they are compared to each other. Since אשת אח is allowed in יבום, the הקש would suggest every ערוה is allowed in יבום too. ״עָלֶיהָ״ blocks this by teaching that a wife's sister stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison drawn from two things the תורה puts side by side
Forbidden relations
A brother's wife, permitted through יבום
Is permitted
'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה

steps.whyThisMatters: This reason does not depend on the order of events. It explains why ״עָלֶיהָ״ is needed in every case, not just one narrow setup.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
it would come through the juxtaposition of Rabbi Yona.
phrases.notes: He means: without ״עָלֶיהָ״, the idea that forbidden relations are permitted in יבום would have come from this comparison.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yona said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua:
The verse states:

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי כׇּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה מִכֹּל הַתּוֹעֵבוֹת הָאֵלֶּה וְנִכְרְתוּ״,
phrases.english: "For whoever shall do any of these abominations… shall be cut off,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:29

phrases.aramaic: הוּקְשׁוּ כׇּל הָעֲרָיוֹת כּוּלָּן לְאֵשֶׁת אָח:
phrases.english: all the forbidden relations are juxtaposed with a brother's wife:
just as a brother's wife is permitted,
phrases.notes: She is permitted in a יבום case, when the brother died without children.

phrases.english: so too all forbidden relations are also permitted;
therefore the Merciful One wrote "with her."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: אָתְיָא בְּהֶיקֵּישָׁא מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent reason why ״עָלֶיהָ״ was needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative source for the mistaken thought (a הקש instead of a מגו)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of רבי יונה's הקש, all עריות would be permitted in יבום, like אשת אח
steps.terutzMaskana: ״עָלֶיהָ״ teaches that a wife's sister, and through her the other עריות, stay forbidden

steps.title: רב אחא of Difti: why compare to the wife's sister and not to the brother's wife?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי asks רבינא: the עריות could be compared either to אשת אח (permitted) or to אחות אשה (forbidden). Why choose אחות אשה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא of Difti said to רבינא: all the forbidden relations could be compared to a brother's wife, and they could also be compared to a wife's sister. Why did you compare them to a wife's sister? Compare them to a brother's wife!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא attacks the הקש approach. He points out that the comparison could go in two opposite directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After ״עָלֶיהָ״ forbids אחות אשה, there are two models: אשת אח, which is permitted in יבום, and אחות אשה, which is forbidden. Comparing the other עריות to אחות אשה makes them forbidden. Comparing them to אשת אח makes them permitted. רב אחא wants to know what makes the strict choice correct.

keyTerms.meaning: To compare them by הקש
A wife's sister
'What did you see?', meaning why choose this side over the other

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
After all, all forbidden relations,
one could compare them to a brother's wife,
and one could compare them to a wife's sister.
What did you see that you compared them to a wife's sister?
Compare them to a brother's wife!
phrases.notes: If we did that, the other forbidden relations would come out permitted in יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: מִכְּדִי כֹּל עֲרָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the direction of the הקש used in Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to compare all עריות to אחות אשה rather than to אשת אח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הקש works equally well in either direction, so choosing the strict model seems to have no reason behind it

steps.title: First answer: when a comparison could go either way, we go strict
steps.stepSummary: When a הקש could lead either to a קולא or to a חומרא, we compare in the strict direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say: when it could go lenient or strict, we compare in the strict direction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to רב אחא. When the choice is unclear, we choose the strict side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both comparisons are possible, the tie is broken by a rule: compare לחומרא. So the עריות are compared to אחות אשה and stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A lenient result
A strict result
We compare by הקש

phrases.english: If you wish, say: when it is between lenient and strict,
we compare in the strict direction.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְקוּלָּא וְחוּמְרָא — לְחוּמְרָא מַקְּשִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's question with a general rule for breaking the tie
steps.terutzResolutionType: General rule for deciding the direction of a הקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison could equally go to אשת אח and permit
steps.terutzMaskana: When a הקש could go either way, we choose the strict side, so the עריות are forbidden

steps.title: Second answer: a case of two prohibitions is learned from another case of two prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: A ערוה who falls to יבום has two prohibitions, just like a wife's sister who is also a brother's wife. Plain יבום has only one prohibition, אשת אח, and two prohibitions are not learned from one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: here there are two prohibitions and there there are two prohibitions, and we learn two from two. But in plain יבום there is only one prohibition, and we do not learn two from one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, more exact answer to רב אחא. It shows that the two cases really are not equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any other ערוה who falls to יבום carries two prohibitions: אשת אח plus her own ערוה. A wife's sister in a יבום case also carries two: אשת אח plus אחות אשה. A plain brother's wife carries only one. So the right match is with אחות אשה, and the result is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Two prohibitions
One prohibition
We learn or derive

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons the עריות are compared to אחות אשה and stay forbidden in יבום. First, we choose the strict side. Second, a case with two prohibitions matches another case with two, not a case with only one.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'here' (הָכָא) is used three times for different cases. The first two mean a wife's sister in יבום and another ערוה in יבום, each with two prohibitions. The last one means plain יבום, with only one prohibition.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
here there are two prohibitions,
phrases.notes: This is the wife's sister who is also a brother's widow: אשת אח plus אחות אשה.

phrases.english: and here there are two prohibitions,
phrases.notes: This is any other forbidden relation who falls to יבום: אשת אח plus her own prohibition.

phrases.english: and we learn two from two.
But here there is one prohibition,
phrases.notes: This is plain יבום, where the only problem is that she was his brother's wife.

phrases.english: and we do not learn two from one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָכָא תְּרֵי אִיסּוּרֵי, וְהָכָא תְּרֵי אִיסּוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to רב אחא's question
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the cases are not equal (matching by number of prohibitions)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עריות could just as well be compared to אשת אח
steps.terutzMaskana: The עריות match אחות אשה (two prohibitions), not plain אשת אח (one), so they stay forbidden

steps.title: רבא: the verse is needed for the rival wife, not the forbidden relative
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a ערוה needs no פסוק to be excluded from יבום, because an עשה does not override a לאו with כרת. So ״עָלֶיהָ״ is needed to forbid the צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A forbidden relative does not need a verse, because a positive מצוה does not override a prohibition that carries כרת. The verse was needed to forbid the rival wife.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a whole new way to explain what ״עָלֶיהָ״ teaches. He says it is not about the ערוה herself at all, but about her צרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערוה is already blocked by a general rule: the מצוה of יבום (an עשה) cannot push aside an איסור כרת. Since that is already known, the פסוק ״עָלֶיהָ״ would be extra for her. So it must teach something new, that the צרה is forbidden too, even though the צרה is not a relative of the יבם.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman forbidden to the man as a close relative (an ערוה relationship)
A positive commandment, here the מצוה of יבום
A prohibition whose punishment is כרת (spiritual cutting off)
Rival wife, meaning the other wife of the dead brother
To forbid

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is permitting the ערוה. He agrees she is forbidden. He just says we already know that from a general rule, so the פסוק must be teaching about the צרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the question from the ערוה herself to her צרה, the subject of the whole first perek of יבמות. The next steps test this view. In step 22 it is restated more precisely: in רבא's name, even the צרה needs no פסוק.

phrases.english: Rava said:
a forbidden relative does not need a verse,
phrases.notes: He means there's no need for a פסוק to tell us she can't do יבום.

phrases.english: because a positive commandment does not override
a prohibition that carries כרת.
where the verse was needed
is to forbid the rival wife.
phrases.notes: The verse is ״עָלֶיהָ״, the same word discussed in the earlier steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: עֶרְוָה לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier explanations (steps 5-9) of why ״עָלֶיהָ״ is needed for the ערוה, with a new explanation that it teaches the צרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ערוה is excluded from יבום by the general rule that an עשה does not override a לאו with כרת. ״עָלֶיהָ״ comes to forbid the צרה.

steps.title: Challenge: the baraita derives the forbidden relative herself from the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבא can say the ערוה needs no פסוק, when the ברייתא says ״אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הִיא״, which implies the פסוק teaches about her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a forbidden relative doesn't need a verse? But it was taught: 'I have only her!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase ״אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הִיא״ suggests the פסוק taught the law of the ערוה herself, and then the ברייתא looks for a further source for her צרה. That seems to show the ערוה does need a פסוק, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I have only…', a formula meaning the פסוק so far teaches only this case
But isn't it so that…, which opens a challenge

phrases.english: And a forbidden relative doesn't need a verse?
But isn't it taught:
'I have only her!'
phrases.notes: Meaning: the verse so far teaches only about the ערוה herself, and then the ברייתא asks where we learn her צרה from.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעֶרְוָה לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's claim using the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that ״עֶרְוָה לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's ״אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הִיא״ implies the פסוק is the source for the ערוה herself.

steps.title: Answer: the baraita mentions her only because of her rival wife
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא mentions the ערוה only as a lead-in to its real point, the צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of her rival wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. The ברייתא says ״הִיא״ only to set up the discussion of her צרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not mean the ערוה's law comes from this פסוק. It names her only so that it can move on to the new teaching, that the צרה is also forbidden. So רבא's reading still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of; for the sake of
Her rival wife
The rival wife of a forbidden relative, who is also exempt from יבום

phrases.english: Because of her rival wife.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא says 'her' only to set up the real lesson about the צרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's wording as a lead-in, not a derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הִיא״ means the פסוק is the source for the ערוה herself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ערוה is mentioned only as a setup for the צרה, which is what the פסוק really teaches.

steps.title: Second challenge: the baraita says 'I have only them'
steps.stepSummary: Another line of the ברייתא, ״אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הֵן״, again seems to make the women themselves the subject of the derivation.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches: 'I have only them!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second wording challenge from a different line of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the ברייתא uses the plural ״הֵן״, 'them', for the forbidden women it listed. Again it sounds like the פסוק is the source for the women themselves, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches; the ברייתא states
They / them, here the forbidden women
'I have only them', meaning the פסוק so far covers only these women

phrases.english: But it teaches:
'I have only them!'
phrases.notes: 'Them' are the forbidden women listed in the ברייתא, such as the sisters.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָתָנֵי: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same kind of challenge as step 11, using a second line of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that ״עֶרְוָה לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ״אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הֵן״ again implies the פסוק teaches the law of the forbidden women themselves.

steps.title: Answer: again, it is said because of their rival wives
steps.stepSummary: Same answer as before. ״הֵן״ is mentioned only to lead into the law of their צרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of their rival wives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge the same way as the first, and רבא's reading holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as ״הִיא״ was only a lead-in to her צרה, ״הֵן״ is only a lead-in to their צרות. The real teaching of ״עָלֶיהָ״ stays the same: the צרות are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Their rival wives
Rival wives (plural)
Exempt from יבום

steps.whatToRemember: So far, according to רבא, a ערוה is excluded from יבום by the general rule that an עשה does not override a לאו with כרת. The ברייתא names the ערוה (״הִיא״, ״הֵן״) only to lead into the law of the צרה. Step 22 later restates רבא more precisely: even the צרה needs no פסוק.

phrases.english: Because of their rival wives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 using the same idea as step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's wording as a lead-in, not a derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הֵן״ means the פסוק is the source for the forbidden women themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The women are mentioned only to set up the law of their צרות, so רבא's view stands.

steps.title: רבי's ברייתא says the extra words forbid both צרות and עריות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי learning from ״וּלְקָחָהּ״ and ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ that צרות and עריות are both forbidden. This suggests that the ערוה herself needs a פסוק, against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי says, the פסוק could have said 'take' but says 'take her,' and could have said 'do יבום' but says 'do יבום with her.' These extra words come to forbid rival wives and forbidden relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to challenge רבא again. In this ברייתא, רבי says the extra words in the פסוק forbid both the צרות and the עריות themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the ערוה needs no פסוק, because an עשה cannot push aside a לאו that carries כרת. Here רבי openly names 'עריות' as one of the things the extra words forbid. So it looks like the ערוה does need a פסוק after all.

keyTerms.meaning: And take her. The extra 'her' points to this specific woman.
And do יבום with her. Again, the extra 'her' is used to learn a limit.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rebbi says:
[Not just] "and take" but "and take her,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5. The extra letter ה, meaning 'her,' is what רבי is learning from.

phrases.english: [not just] "and do יבום" but "and do יבום with her" —
to forbid rival wives and forbidden relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new challenge to רבא from a different ברייתא, after the answers in steps 12 and 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that a ערוה needs no פסוק to be excluded from יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי names עריות as something the extra words forbid. That means the ערוה does need a פסוק.

steps.title: Read the ברייתא as the rival wives of the forbidden relatives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי's words as 'צרות של עריות,' meaning the rival wives of the forbidden relatives. Read this way, the ערוה herself is not taught here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: to forbid the rival wives of the forbidden relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by changing how we read the ברייתא. It does not say 'צרות and עריות' but 'צרות של עריות.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, both extra words are about only one thing, the צרה. The ערוה herself is still forbidden with no פסוק, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead. The גמרא suggests a different reading of the source.
The rival wives of the forbidden relatives.

phrases.english: Say instead: to forbid the rival wives of the forbidden relatives.
phrases.notes: The גמרא changes 'צרות and עריות' to 'צרות of עריות,' so the ברייתא is only talking about the rival wives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15 by rereading the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי learned two separate laws: one forbidding the צרה and one forbidding the ערוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי learned only one law, forbidding the צרה of the ערוה.

steps.title: Why would רבי need two extra words for one law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. רבי brought two extra words, which suggests two laws: one for the ערוה and one for the צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he brought two words from the פסוק. Isn't it that one is for the ערוה and one is for the צרה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from step 16. If רבי only meant the צרה, why did he need two extra words?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate words usually mean two separate laws. The easy match is one word for the ערוה and one for the צרה. That would bring us right back to the problem with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Two words or phrases from a פסוק. Literally, 'two verses.'
He is bringing, or taking, for himself.
Isn't it that...? This introduces the conclusion the questioner thinks is obvious.

phrases.english: But he is bringing two words from the פסוק,
phrases.notes: The two words are ״וּלְקָחָהּ״ and ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ from step 15.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו: חַד לְעֶרְוָה וְחַד לְצָרָה?
phrases.english: isn't it that one is for the forbidden relative and one is for the rival wife?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rereading offered in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'צרות של עריות' from step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two extra words imply two laws. The natural split is one word for the ערוה and one for the צרה.

steps.title: Both words are about the צרה, one forbidding and one permitting
steps.stepSummary: Both words teach about the צרה. One forbids the צרה where there is a מצוה of יבום. The other permits her where there is no מצוה of יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Both are about the rival wife. One forbids the rival wife where there is a מצוה of יבום, and one permits the rival wife where there is no מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second word is not for the ערוה. Both words deal with the צרה, but they teach two different laws about her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first word forbids the צרה of a ערוה from doing יבום with the brother. The second word limits that rule to cases where there is a מצוה of יבום. In any other case, the צרה is allowed to marry that man after her husband dies.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both of them.
In a case where there is a מצוה, here meaning the מצוה of יבום.
To forbid.
To permit.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'permit a צרה' as permitting יבום with her. It means that outside a יבום case, such as when her husband was not this man's brother, the צרה of his relative may marry him.

phrases.english: No, this one and that one are both for the rival wife:
one is to forbid the rival wife where there is a mitzvah [of יבום],

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לְמִישְׁרֵי צָרָה שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹם מִצְוָה.
phrases.english: and one is to permit the rival wife where there is no מצוה.
phrases.notes: He means a case where her dead husband was not this man's brother, so there is no יבום at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by giving the second word a different job, still about the צרה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives each extra word a separate law about the same subject.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two words must mean one for the ערוה and one for the צרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both words are about the צרה. One forbids her in a יבום case, and one permits her outside a יבום case. So רבא still stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a real halachic limit: the special איסור on a צרה applies only in a יבום case.

steps.title: How ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ teaches that the איסור applies only in a יבום case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the source for the permitting law. The word ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ shows that the צרה is forbidden only where there is יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The פסוק says 'do יבום with her' and not just 'do יבום.' Only where there is יבום is the rival wife forbidden. Where there is no יבום, the rival wife is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the second law from step 18 and answers it at once. The word ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ ties the צרה איסור to the setting of יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the extra word mentions יבום, the איסור on the צרה belongs only inside יבום. Outside a יבום case, there is nothing to forbid her. This finishes the defense of רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? Here it asks for the source.
She is forbidden.
She is permitted.

steps.whatToRemember: רבא stands. The ערוה herself needs no פסוק. רבי's two extra words both teach about the צרה: forbidden in a יבום case, and permitted outside a יבום case.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
[Not just] "and do יבום" but "and do יבום with her":
it is in a case of יבום that the rival wife is forbidden;
in a case that is not יבום, the rival wife is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the permitting law stated in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which word teaches that the צרה is permitted outside a יבום case, and how.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ limits the צרה איסור to cases of יבום, so outside יבום she is permitted.

steps.title: רב אשי finds support for רבא in the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points out that the משנה says the women 'exempt their צרות' but never says they 'are exempt.' This shows their own exemption is obvious, just as רבא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording of the משנה also fits this. It says, 'Fifteen women exempt their rival wives.' It does not say, 'They are exempt and they exempt.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support for רבא from the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ערוה's own exemption needed a פסוק, it would be a new law, and the משנה would mention it. The משנה only teaches that she exempts her צרה, so the only new law is about the צרה. This fits רבא's view that the ערוה herself needs no פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה is also precise this way, meaning its wording supports the view
They exempt others, here their צרות
They themselves are exempt
Learn from this, a proof is confirmed

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The Mishnah is also precise this way,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's wording fits רבא's view.

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָתָנֵי: חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה נָשִׁים פּוֹטְרוֹת צָרוֹתֵיהֶן.
phrases.english: as it teaches: Fifteen women exempt their rival wives.
whereas 'they are exempt and they exempt' it does not teach.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge from רבי's ברייתא has been answered, רב אשי adds support for רבא from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that the ערוה herself needs no פסוק for her exemption
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'פוטרות צרותיהן' and the absence of 'פטורות ופוטרות'

steps.title: If the forbidden relative needs no verse, why should her rival wife need one?
steps.stepSummary: The ערוה needs no פסוק because a עשה cannot push aside a לאו with כרת. The גמרא asks why that same reason does not also cover the צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes the forbidden relative different, so that she needs no verse? It is because a positive מצוה cannot push aside a prohibition that carries כרת. Then the rival wife should also need no verse, for the very same reason!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא by taking his own reasoning and applying it to the צרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reason is that the מצוה of יבום, a עשה, cannot override a כרת prohibition. The צרה of an ערוה is also forbidden with כרת. So that reason should exempt her too, and the extra words of the פסוק would seem to have nothing left to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It asks why two cases are treated differently
Needs a פסוק as a source

keyTerms.term: אֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כָּרֵת
keyTerms.meaning: A positive command cannot push aside a prohibition that carries כרת
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for the most severe sins

phrases.english: And what is different about a forbidden relative
that she does not need a verse?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כָּרֵת?
phrases.english: Because a positive מצוה does not push aside a prohibition that carries karet?
A rival wife too should not need a verse,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כָּרֵת!
phrases.english: because a positive מצוה does not push aside a prohibition that carries karet!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא עֶרְוָה דְּלָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Right after רבא's view has been supported, the גמרא tests whether his reasoning proves too much.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the פסוק is needed for the צרה but not for the ערוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason the ערוה needs no פסוק, that a עשה cannot push aside a כרת prohibition, applies equally to the צרה. So the צרה should not need a פסוק either.

steps.title: רב אחא בר ביבי מר: in רבא's name, the rival wife needs no verse either
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר ביבי מר tells רבינא that רבא's real teaching is that the צרה also needs no פסוק. He then begins to explain where the פסוק is actually needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר ביבי מר said to רבינא: This is what we say in the name of רבא. The rival wife also does not need a verse. Where the verse is needed is...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר ביבי מר answers the challenge by accepting it: the צרה also needs no פסוק. He then begins to explain what the פסוק is really for, and that explanation continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is not pushed away. It is accepted, and רבא's teaching is restated correctly. Both the ערוה and her צרה are forbidden by the כרת rule without any פסוק. So the extra words must teach something else, and that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: This is how we say it, introducing the correct version of a teaching
In the name of רבא
Was needed

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר בִּיבִי מָר לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Bivai Mar said to Ravina:
This is what we say in the name of Rava:
A rival wife also does not need a verse.
Where the verse is needed is...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers step 21 by accepting its point and restating רבא's teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the original teaching correctly, while accepting the challenger's logic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבא said the פסוק was needed to forbid the צרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבא, even the צרה needs no פסוק to be forbidden. The פסוק has a different purpose, which the גמרא is about to explain.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the צרה is permitted. She is still forbidden. The point is only that this prohibition needs no special פסוק, because the כרת rule already covers her.
